focus: Identify accuracy and cost levers from the recorded run: call protocol, usage recording, caching, regex coverage, and grader-path overhead.
noveltyJustification: First recomputation of order stability per row, the usage-recording gap against the client's own response shape, the in-repo cache precedent, and a regex-format probe; all new to this lineage.
keyQuestions: What drove the measured Jev result?
How can accuracy improve or cost fall?
How can the measurement become more trustworthy?
Where else in .skilled would the same judgment pay off?
What would default-on integration need, cost, and risk?
answeredQuestions: How can accuracy improve or cost fall?
ruledOut: Treat the three-order protocol as free accuracy: F=0 with unanimous picks means the third call added cost, not information, on these rows.
Treat a regex widening as measurable on the current corpus: it avoids every verdict token by construction.
Treat the printed token estimate as measured cost: it is a pre-run character heuristic.
focusTrackReason: Cost and accuracy levers follow directly from iteration 1's result decomposition and the recorded calls.

title: The protocol costs 3 calls per miss plus an auth call, serially
claim: 73 planned calls for 24 rows at p50 334 ms and 16,767 estimated tokens; cost is linear in fallback volume times three.

title: Order rotation bought no accuracy on this corpus
claim: All 24 rows show identical picks across the three option orders with F=0 and modal top=3; the lowest pick probability is 0.96, so one call per row and a confirm-on-uncertainty protocol would both have used 24 calls here.

title: Cost is unrecorded even though the client reports usage
claim: calls.jsonl drops the jev response's usage.input_tokens/output_tokens; the only cost figure is a ceil(chars/4) pre-run estimate and the auth test is an unrecorded billed call.

title: A cache precedent exists in the same pipeline and is unused here
claim: The eval rig has an append-only cache keyed by input bundle and grader model hash with run-scoped roots; the fallback records none, so reruns re-pay every call even though requalify provides the invalidation seam.

title: The regex is narrower than plausible natural formats and this corpus cannot price a widening
claim: Bold, heading-prefixed, adjective-prefixed, em-dash and trailing-content verdict lines all miss extractVerdict while plain prefixed lines hit; the measured corpus avoids every verdict token, so widening must be priced on a natural corpus.

title: The production grader path is process-heavy versus the hosted Jev arm
claim: --grader llm dispatches cli-opencode or cli-claude-code with a 600 s default timeout, while the measured Jev call is hosted at p50 334 ms; a Jev grader backend keeps the three-key contract and drops process overhead.
